content.text:
I'm mapping the grid layout: the source yellow marker sits in island (row 2, col 1), while the target cyan marker is in island (row 1, col 2). I'm checking the gate positions around the source island to figure out the connecting path from there.

Following the gates, (2,1) connects to (1,1) and (2,0), but (1,1) only leads onward to (0,1) and (1,0), not the target. Tracing which islands can reach (1,2) directly, only (0,2) has a downward gate into it, so I need a path through (0,2), which in turn is reachable only from (0,3), which is reachable only from (1,3), which requires checking whether (2,3) connects upward into it.

Tracing further from the original source, (2,1)->(1,1) branches to (0,1) or (1,0); (0,1) leads to (0,0) or back to (1,1); (1,0) leads to (0,0) or (2,0); (2,0) leads down to (3,0); (0,0) loops back to (1,0); and (3,0) leads right to (3,1) -- none of these branches seem to connect into the (2,3)/(1,3)/(0,3)/(0,2)/(1,2) chain I need.

I'm now trying the other direction from (3,1): it connects to (2,1), (3,0), or (3,2); (3,2) connects to (2,2) or (3,3); (3,3) connects to (2,3); (2,3) connects to (1,3) or back to (2,2); (1,3) leads up to (0,3); (0,3) leads left to (0,2); and (0,2) finally drops down to (1,2), which is the target -- so there's a valid path (2,1)→(3,1)→(3,2)→(3,3)→(2,3)→(1,3)→(0,3)→(0,2)→(1,2), though I also considered a longer alternate route through (2,0) and (3,0) that isn't as efficient.

Now I'm mapping out the exact gate coordinates along path A, translating each move into its grid position, so I can trace the full route from the source center to the target cell precisely.

I should craft a few valid test inputs, reusing the given example as one and building smaller ones myself. I'm sketching a small 2x2 lattice grid with islands placed at specific rows and columns, working out where centers and gates go for each island.

Building the grid layout...

Now I'm planning a couple more demo grids beyond this one, including reusing the original example, to have a set of varied test cases.

For a third demo, I decide on a 3x3 lattice using a different border color to demonstrate that colors can vary. I lay out a 13x13 grid with islands at rows/columns 1, 5, 9, placing a yellow source at the bottom-left and cyan target at top-right, with a minimal length-4 path going up twice then right twice, confirming there's no shorter route.

I need to be careful about extra gates I add elsewhere, since a stray gate at (1,1) could create an alternate length-4 path and break uniqueness -- so I place non-helpful gates instead, like a left gate at (1,1) and up gate at (2,2). Then I start writing out the actual grid rows for the islands with their borders, centers, and midpoints.

Writing island grid rows...

Still mapping out grid values...

I verify the (2,2)U path leads to a dead end at (1,2) with no gates, so it's fine. All three grids check out and are ready to submit.
